description: Shapes that travel in more than one contract, so that the generator has something to import.

A vocabulary declares no ops and no errors: nobody produces one and nobody calls it. What it is for here is the cross-file half of the emitter — a type used in one file and declared in another is the only thing an import statement can be tested on.

types.name: Direction
description: Which way an event travelled. Imported rather than restated, so that both contracts are documented as speaking the same set.

variants.name: input
description: From the caller. The wire value is shorter than the name, which is the whole reason the two are separate keys.

types.name: Meta
description: When an event happened and which way it went.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
description: Milliseconds since the epoch, assigned by the producer. A wall-clock millisecond count sits many orders of magnitude inside the safe range, so it is declared exact rather than wide.
